facts.fact: The DGPF holds both registers: birth, marriage and death records are being archived electronically in the national database it also uses for identity-card enrolment, and children born abroad must have their birth transcribed before applying for the card.

DJI.note: No count or share of people enrolled.
The NNI is assigned at biometric enrolment, not at birth registration.

facts.fact: The DGPF's own agents run enrolment, checks and duplicate resolution on the national register, according to the head of its central NNI service.

DJI.note: No public register stated as keyed on the NNI.

facts.fact: At enrolment the system automatically assigns each citizen a National Identification Number (NNI) held in the national register, per the DGPF.
Fingerprints, iris and photograph are captured and automatically compared with the database, which has detected duplicates and people using a dead person's identity, says the head of the NNI service.
